Welcome to Episode 02 of Agent Wars. Today we’re challenging 5 top AI models to design, engineer and 3D print a bridge with the goal of holding the most possible weight. ChatGPT and Claude look at information, reason through it, and generate text. Jev looks at the same type of information and makes a small decision fast. One engineer replaced ChatGPT Luna with Jev for a classification task. The engineer reported results 5 to 18 times faster, with greater accuracy. This matters because many AI agent workflows rely on repeated classification and routing decisions. Generating extra tokens adds work when the workflow only needs a label, score, route, or yes/no answer. Jev fits tasks such as sorting inputs into categories, choosing which workflow handles a request, ranking or scoring an item, and detecting spam, risk, intent, urgency, topic, or sentiment. The simple rule: use a general LLM when you need language. Use Jev when you need probabilities for a focused classification or routing decision. What is the Jev AI model? Follow me and DM me "TIMELINE" on IG/FB only 👇 ChatGPT power words give you 5 visual ways to explore a topic. Each command tells ChatGPT how to organize the answer. Paste the exact slash command anywhere in your prompt, then add the topic you want to explore. Here are 5 power words for ChatGPT: 1. /timelineview - create a visual timeline, e.g. historical event 2. /anime-explainer - turn any topic into an anime to remember it 3. /visualcheatsheet - create a 1 pager visual cheat sheet on any topic 4. /explodedview - schematic showing the parts of an object or concept 5. /mindmap - create a mindmap that shows how ideas are connected Use /timelineview when order over time matters. Pick /anime-explainer when an anime overview would help you remember the topic. Choose /visualcheatsheet when you want a one-page study resource. Use /explodedview when you need to separate an object or concept into its parts. Use /mindmap when you want to see how ideas connect. Start with one command, add your topic, then describe any details you want included. Save this list so every command stays easy to find. What are the best ChatGPT power words? How to become the AI person on your team Most people use AI at work like a smarter search bar: paste something in, ask, copy the answer out. Soon that's as common as knowing email. The people getting noticed build with it. They connect AI to the tools their team already uses. Here's one real example, the weekly sales report that eats someone's Monday morning: The doors. Almost every work app (HubSpot, Jira, Google Sheets, Slack) has an API, a door other software can use. No code needed. n8n. Each door becomes a box on a canvas. A schedule trigger fires every Monday at 7, HubSpot pulls last week's deals, Jira counts open tickets, Sheets brings the target, and one AI step has Claude write the report. Context. Give Claude one page about your team: who reads the report, the quarterly target, and that your manager wants bad news first. Now it sounds like your team, not a stranger. Approval. The draft comes to you in Slack first. Tap approve and it posts to the team at 8. Claude Code. For questions that need judgment ("why did the Acme deal slip?"), plug the same tools into Claude Code. It checks HubSpot, Jira and Slack by itself and answers with sources. The rule to keep: if the steps never change, build it in n8n. If the work needs judgment, give it to Claude Code. It takes a few weekends: learn how APIs work, learn one tool all the way down, then connect your first chore. I teach all of it from zero inside my community, seven courses in order.
